description: A product declares at intake how much of it is user interface: none, light or central (rcf discover intake --ui, or rcf discover journey declare). The declaration is written by the tool onto rcf/discovery/journey.json, a sidecar the walker never reads (the rcf/define/ ledger pattern, ADR-4121). For a light or central product the discovery pack carries a journey record: every entry, exit, interruption and return path as steps, each step naming the screen it lands on. The record is JSON written only by the tool; the person authors markdown (the line grammar through rcf discover journey add --from, or the ux-designer journey-map prose shape through rcf discover journey import --from) and the tool mints JNY and SCR ids that stay stable by slug across re-mints. rcf discover journey show prints the record with a derived state per step. rcf discover journey check evaluates structure (a journey with an entry and an exit, every step naming a screen that resolves, every step reachable with no dead end), the interruption catalogue v1 (lostEmail, closedTab, deadBattery, expiredLink, switchedDevice, lostSignal: each answered by an interruption step or ruled out as notApplicable with a reason of at least 20 characters; the check is answered, not drawn) and, for a central product only, one wireframe file per journey step. Wireframes are files in the pack under rcf/discovery/wireframes/: markdown by default, self-contained HTML accepted (no external stylesheet, script, image or font URL), PNG for as-built migration; the gate hashes bytes and never inspects headings; links never satisfy the gate. rcf discover journey review --by seals the record with a sha256 content hash over the canonical record and every wireframe file, refuses on any structural failure, and goes stale on any edit; one reviewer in this release. Readiness gains stage D0 (gate define.discovery, short name discovery) ahead of D1: blocking, never ackable, productOwner on every check, notApplicable for a none product and for a grandfathered tree (no journey.json; existing trees land as they are, with no rollout mechanism, and rcf doctor reports the missing declaration as advice only). The DEFINE door is the three chain-write verbs (rcf define ledger brief add, rcf define create, rcf define blueprint add): on a light or central product whose D0 fails they refuse with exit 4 before any write, in the message family the other gates use; repair verbs stay ungated; a light product is never refused for a missing wireframe. Build units bind to journey steps through an optional FBS journeyStepIds[] (the one field that needs rcf-schemas 0.7); rcf build queue and journey show derive a state per step (unbound, queued, inProgress, built, verified), rcf build bundle prints the bound steps to the executor, and rcf build review reports unbound steps and unbound UI-bearing build specs as findings with no new hard gate at BUILD. Journey steps are discovery evidence: never a node in PRD to REQ to US to AC to TS to TC, never walked by coverage, trace or impact.
rationale: The operator ruling (relayed 2026-10-09): UX design is part of DISCOVERY; DEFINE draws requirements from it; a UI app with no UX, design or wireframing work is rejected at DEFINE. The incident behind it: a product built with rcf-lite had every screen designed per build unit but nobody drew the path between them; wireframes were a per-component sub-task inside DEFINE, never per journey, never owner-reviewed; the result was a 40-question wall with no way back for a lost email or an abandoned session. The product owner posture that shapes the gate (DISCOVERY verdict, same day): the gate is not tight; three values rather than a boolean; the interruption questions matter more than any specific set of wireframes, so wireframe richness is better discovery input and never mandated input; only a central product is ever refused for a missing wireframe; existing trees land safely as they are.
title: UX intake gate: journey record, three-valued UI declaration, D0 discovery stage and the DEFINE door

operatorOverride.reason: DEFINE 2026-10-09: this requirement is CLI verbs, a readiness stage and a tool-written sidecar file; the screen, wireframe, email, session and HTML words describe the product under intake, not a surface this requirement exposes. No HTTP route, no auth, no notification, no web UI, no data store; the same posture REQ-186 and REQ-188 carry (none). Keyword scan is the prompt, not the authority.
